content: Do README files as in cslib#556 appear correctly in the generated docs?
I don’t think they are counted. Let’s check with @Henrik Böving

Thanks. Then, @Ching-Tsun Chou, it'd be good to put the contents of that file somewhere else, in a Lean file. Even a Readme.lean or FLP.lean could be ok.

But feel free to do this in a later PR.
Why not just put it in the appropriate module and section docstrings?

The doc-strings in each Lean file of Cslib/Computability/Distributed/FLP are already self-contained and do not refer to or depend on the README. The README just provides an additional overview that would be useful to those who wish to read the code. There are similar README files in mathlib:

Mathlib README files

Mathlib/Order/README.md
Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Cone/README.md
Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/README.md
Mathlib/Probability/Combinatorics/README.md
Mathlib/Geometry/Group/Growth/README.md
Mathlib/Geometry/Group/README.md
Mathlib/Geometry/Convex/Cone/README.md
Mathlib/Geometry/Convex/README.md
Mathlib/Algebra/README.md
Mathlib/Algebra/Notation/README.md

But I will update the README to clarify that all Lean files except Algorithm.lean are yet to appear in future PRs.

:point_right: On second thought, I decided to add the file Consensus.lean to this PR as well. The two files together can be thought of as a formalization of the problem statement in the original FLP paper, so it is probably better to read them together.
